steps.title: The clock uses different numbers
body: Counting 11-99 used cardinal numbers. Telling time switches to ordinals instead — second, third, fourth — agreeing with السَّاعَة (the hour), which is feminine: السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ, "it's two o'clock", literally "the hour, the second one". No verb needed, the same way English can just answer "two o'clock".

One o'clock breaks the pattern on purpose: there's no "الأُولَى o'clock" — it uses الْوَاحِدَة, the ordinary cardinal "one", instead. Eleven and twelve compound an ordinal with the teen-marker exactly like the cardinal numbers did, and stay fixed on the same ending no matter what — one more place the two systems echo each other.

For minutes, وَ means "past" (السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالنِّصْف, half past two) and إِلَّا means "to" (السَّاعَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا, quarter to four) — two small words carrying real weight.

steps.title: One o'clock to quarter to four
steps.intro: Read each ordinal, then the six clock-time sentences. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: The one exception
steps.prompt: Why الْوَاحِدَة here, not an ordinal like the other hours?

options.label: One o'clock is the exception — it uses the cardinal, not an ordinal
It's a mistake — it should be الأُولَى

steps.explanation: Every other hour uses an ordinal (الثَّانِيَة، الثَّالِثَة…), but one o'clock keeps the cardinal الْوَاحِدَة — there's no "الأُولَى o'clock".

steps.title: Past or to?
steps.explanation: إِلَّا ("except / minus") subtracts from the hour — الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا is "four minus a quarter", i.e. quarter to four. وَ would mean "past" instead.

steps.title: Why ـَ, not ـُ?
steps.prompt: Two o'clock was السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ, ending ـُ. Why does twelve o'clock end ـَ instead?

options.label: 11th/12th are indeclinable, fixed on ـَ regardless of case — like the cardinal teens
It's a typo — it should also end ـُ

steps.explanation: Just like the cardinal teens (11-19) stay fixed on ـَ no matter their case, the ordinal teen-compounds الْحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ and الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ do too — one more place counting numbers and clock numbers rhyme.

steps.title: You can tell the time
steps.message: You've now met all three of Arabic's number systems: cardinals for counting, and ordinals for the clock — with one o'clock, eleven, and twelve each bending the pattern in their own small way. Dates and prices build on these same ordinals and cardinals later.
